votes.evidence:
It is true that the GitHub fetch runs before the dedupe check. In products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1155-1165, `get_pr` runs before the head-keyed ReviewRun check at 1201-1219. The comment at 1152-1154 says this is on purpose: the dedupe needs the PR's current head, and only GitHub knows it. What the finding gets wrong is how often this happens.

1. The receiver drops most saves before any work. In products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:79-88, it returns early on create, on any `update_fields` save that does not include "output", and on FAILED or CANCELLED runs. So state and status saves never refire, including the follow-up state saves the finding names. For example, models.py:1234 saves status, environment, state and updated_at, and models.py:1533 saves status and completed_at. Neither touches output.
2. The Stamphog task is queued only if the acting reviewer's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle is on (receivers.py:131). The task then returns before fetching when no enabled, synced repo config exists (tasks.py:1144-1149).
3. Only these writes save output with the PR URL: the output PATCH in facade/api.py `update_task_run` (1989+), `set_task_run_output` (2139-2154), and the webhook backstop in webhooks.py:292. The agent server syncs `head_branch` only on turns where the branch changed (receivers.py docstring, lines 27-29). So a PR gets a handful of refires, not one per turn.
4. The receiver docstring at receivers.py:73-77 accepts this cost on purpose: "a same-head re-trigger costs one fetch (early-exit)". The task docstring at tasks.py:1124-1128 explains that refetching lets the task review a new head whose synchronize webhook was lost. The suggested TTL cache would give up part of that recovery to save a few GET calls.
5. Rate limits are already handled: `GitHubRateLimitError` retries with a backoff of at least 60s (tasks.py:1160-1162). A few calls per PR are negligible next to a GitHub App installation's hourly limit.

The result is an accepted, documented design tradeoff with low real frequency. It is not a defect.
votes.refutation: The claim of "a steady stream across many turns" does not match the code. The receiver ignores every save that does not write output (receivers.py:83-86). Only a few writes set output.pr_url, and the branch sync runs only when the branch changes. The Stamphog leg is also behind a toggle and a repo-config check. Fetching before the dedupe is the documented design (tasks.py:1152-1154, receivers.py:73-77): the dedupe needs GitHub's current head, and refetching recovers a lost synchronize webhook. Each extra refire costs one GET, and the rate-limit backoff is already handled (tasks.py:1160-1162). At most this is a minor efficiency preference with no defect that ships.

votes.evidence:
The code does work the way the finding says. In products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1155-1164, process_inbox_pr_review calls StamphogGitHubClient.get_pr before it checks for duplicates, and the duplicate check keys on head_sha (1199-1216). The receiver in products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:79-130 queues this task on every TaskRun save that carries output.pr_url. But the claimed defect is only a guess about cost, and it is a tradeoff the author chose and wrote down.
(1) Both docstrings name this cost as accepted: "a same-head re-trigger costs one fetch (early-exit)" (receivers.py:71-76), and the task docstring at tasks.py:1124-1128 explains that the fetch comes first because only GitHub knows the current head. The comment at tasks.py:1153-1154 repeats this.
(2) The receiver already filters out most saves before any queueing. It returns on created (82-84), on update_fields without "output" (85-89, which skips follow-up state and status saves), on FAILED or CANCELLED runs, on non-signal tasks, on internal tasks, when no reviewer resolves, and when the stamphog toggle is off (109-130). The saves that remain are output writes. There are only a few paths that write output: set_task_run_output (tasks facade/api.py:2154), the PATCH output merge (api.py:~2043), and the webhook backstop (webhooks.py:292). So the refire count per PR is a few per agent turn at most, which is far below GitHub's per-installation hourly quota.
(3) Rate limits are already handled. GitHubRateLimitError retries with a countdown of max(retry_after, 60) (tasks.py:1159-1161), so quota pressure delays the review but loses nothing.
(4) Tests cover this refire and dedupe behavior on purpose: test_inbox_receiver_leg_refires_dedupe_on_the_current_head (products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:992-1050), plus the closed-PR refire case (~1052).
(5) The suggested TTL cache would suppress refires within its window. That weakens recovery from a lost synchronize event, which the docstring names as the reason for the fetch.
The claimed rate-limit harm has no shown trigger, and the cost is a documented design choice, so this is not a real defect.
votes.refutation: The extra fetch per refire is a documented, deliberate tradeoff (receivers.py:71-76, tasks.py:1124-1128 and 1153-1154). The receiver drops saves that don't write output before queueing (receivers.py:85-89), rate-limit errors retry with a countdown (tasks.py:1159-1161), and tests pin the refire and dedupe behavior (test_tasks.py:992). Adding a TTL cache would weaken recovery from a lost synchronize event, and nothing shows the extra fetches reaching the GitHub quota.

votes.evidence:
The fetch-before-dedupe order is real: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1155-1164 calls StamphogGitHubClient.get_pr before the head-keyed ReviewRun dedupe at 1199-1219. The finding says this becomes "a steady stream" of API calls, one per agent turn. The code does not support that.
(1) Receiver filter, products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:77-86. It returns early when the row was just created. It also returns early when update_fields is given and does not include "output". The code comment says follow-up state saves and status flips are dropped with no DB hit. So state, status and turn-end saves that leave `output` alone never queue the stamphog task.
(2) In production, `output` is written in only three places: products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2040-2045 (the PATCH output merge), api.py:2153-2154 (set_task_run_output), and products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:291-292 (the webhook backstop, which writes pr_url). No bare run.save() without update_fields exists in products/tasks/backend.
(3) The agent syncs head_branch only on turns where the git branch changed (receivers.py:27-28; DECISIONS.md:2554). pr_url is written once by the agent, plus at most one backstop write.
So a run gets a handful of refires in its lifetime, not one per turn. Each refire costs one GET on the installation token, and the task already backs off on GitHubRateLimitError (tasks.py:1159-1161).
The stamphog leg is also narrow. It needs the acting reviewer's stamphog_review_inbox_prs toggle to be on (receivers.py:122), and it exits before any fetch when the repo has no enabled, synced StamphogRepoConfig (tasks.py:1136-1152).
The docstrings accept this cost on purpose: receivers.py:73-74 ("a same-head re-trigger costs one fetch (early-exit)") and tasks.py:1125-1129. The fetch has to come first because the lost-synchronize recovery needs the current head.
votes.refutation: The trigger the finding describes ("each turn-end sync, webhook backstop writes, follow-up state saves" causing a steady stream of fetches) is not reachable in production. The receiver drops every save whose update_fields leaves out "output" (receivers.py:80-84). Only three code paths write output (tasks facade api.py:2154, api.py:2045, webhooks.py:292). The agent writes head_branch only when the branch changes, and writes pr_url about once. Refires per PR are therefore few and bounded. Each costs one GitHub GET with rate-limit backoff, a cost the docstring accepts on purpose. Adding a TTL cache would guard against load that does not exist, so this is a speculative efficiency concern with no real trigger.
